drafted_from: workflow:check-a-decision-against-your-map's row in tools/workflows/recipes/workflows.json (its input schema, steps and submit shapes)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:check-a-decision-against-your-map for case_id case:lease-a-second-oven and keep the result on the decision."

lists.label: Your map
lists.holds: One area of the person's life, what it means and what it is part of.

values.means: How well your body is and what you do for it.
The objects, places and resources around you.
The people and animals in your life.

instructions: 1. Pour the example areas into the list where you keep the parts of your life (see pour), or make list:your-map from them.

3. The AI works read, weigh and keep: it reads the decision and your map, says for every area whether the option serves it, leaves it out or takes from it with evidence, and names a better version that also lives an area none of your pursuits touch.
4. Read the note kept on the decision.

worked_examples.title: Leasing a second oven serves money and takes from the body
worked_examples.ask: Weigh the second-oven decision against my map.
worked_examples.given: The read step returned map_areas ["Things, places and money","Your body"] and missing ["Your body"] (no pursuit touches it). The decision text says the lease is 800 a month, adds 40 loaves a day, and the baker would start at 3 AM five days a week. Read from the weigh step of the workflow row.
worked_examples.hands_back: The submit shape of step weigh: {"areas":[{"area":"Things, places and money","effect":"serves","how":"The lease adds 40 loaves a day of capacity against an 800 a month cost.","evidence":[{"where":"case:lease-a-second-oven option A","quote":"adds 40 loaves a day"}]},{"area":"Your body","effect":"takes-from","how":"A 3 AM start five days a week cuts the sleep the person has said they need.","evidence":[{"where":"case:lease-a-second-oven option A","quote":"start at 3 AM five days a week"}]}],"better_version":"Lease the oven but hire a second baker for the early shift so the owner keeps a normal morning."}

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
